title: Minimum Array End
summary: Consider strictly increasing arrays of n positive integers whose bitwise AND is x.

contractDetails.constraints: 1 ≤ n,x ≤ 100000000. Return an exact integer in a signed 64-bit result slot. Under these bounds the result is below 2^53, so JavaScript, TypeScript, and R can use exact numeric arithmetic if they avoid 32-bit bitwise truncation.
contractDetails.output-checking: Return a signed 64-bit integer. Canonical JSON preserves the entire value under the source bounds, which imply result<2^53. JavaScript, TypeScript, and R must avoid 32-bit shifts on the wide result.

statement: Consider strictly increasing arrays of n positive integers whose bitwise AND is x. Return the smallest possible final value. Every array entry must contain every set bit of x.

examples.explanation: The first three supermasks are 10, 11, and 14.
The only element must equal x.
The lowest 26 bits are fixed at one, so the rank is placed above them.

constraints: 1 ≤ n,x ≤ 100000000. Return an exact integer in a signed 64-bit result slot. Under these bounds the result is below 2^53, so JavaScript, TypeScript, and R can use exact numeric arithmetic if they avoid 32-bit bitwise truncation.
hints: Conceptual: Every valid element is a supermask of x, and x itself can be the first element.
Directional: Order the supermasks by filling the zero positions of x.
Implementation: Use n−1 as a binary rank. Deposit its low-to-high bits into the zero positions of x from low to high.
complexityAnalysis: O(log n + log x) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
